messages:
Maya Patel: Heads up — noticed a big delta in EU reserved capacity utilization last night vs what's shown in the finops dashboard. Burn jumped ~45% for GPU hours between 01:00-04:00 UTC. Link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/finops?panel=eu_burn :eyes:
Samir Khan: seen that. any single job or model causing it?
Maya Patel: looks per-model. The top 3 contributors are a longtail of model variants hitting autoscale bursts. Quick snapshot from BQ: ```SELECT model_id, SUM(token_cost) AS cost, SUM(gpu_hours) AS gpu_h FROM `billing.prod.per_route_usage` WHERE region='eu' AND _PARTITIONTIME BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() GROUP BY model_id ORDER BY cost DESC LIMIT 10;```
Raghav Singh: can you paste the results? I can't run BQ from phone.
Maya Patel: pasted results in thread (summary): model-retrieval-v2: $1.9k / 28 GPUh, chat-lite-quant: $1.1k / 16 GPUh, rerank-ensemble: $950 / 12 GPUh. Several smaller models ~ $100-300 each.
Finance Analyst: billing-bot flagged an uncommitted burst: reserved_commitment_eu = 120 GPUh, consumed_peak = 192 GPUh (2026-02-22 03:10 UTC). Invoice preview: https://billing.redwood/reports/2026-02-22/eu-peak
Samir Khan: that gap explains the extra on-demand premium. Are these models configured to fallback to cheaper variants?
Maya Patel: partly. Some routes were recently updated to pin to latest weights (chat-lite-quant) and we didn't add a cold-cache option. Autoscale policy for two deployments uses `burst_to_capacity: true` which lets pods spawn extra GPUs via cloud burst.
Oliver Chen: we had a config push last week from eng-runtime that relaxed `min_replicas` for P95 latency — maybe related. cc @eng-runtime.
Raghav Singh: immediate mitigation: can we temporarily disable burst for those 3 highest-cost routes and spin up a reserve pool? Impact on latency minimal during low qps.
Samir Khan: Agreed. Also recommend adjusting finops dashboard alert thresholds: current threshold triggers at 20% over commitment sustained for 6h. For spike patterns we should add a short-window alert (30m) to catch night surges.
Maya Patel: I'll open a quick patch: set `burst_to_capacity: false` for model-retrieval-v2 and chat-lite-quant and add a cold-cache fallback. Deploying in 10m.
Finance Analyst: note for finance: provisional estimate of incremental on-demand cost for that window is ~$4.2k. We'll put a hold on pass-through to customer bill until we confirm root cause.
billing-bot: [automated] Billing anomaly detected: project=redwood-prod region=eu type=commitment-mismatch severity=high window=2026-02-22T01:30:00Z-2026-02-22T04:15:00Z extra_cost=4200 USD. Case: #BILL-4621 created.
Samir Khan: long-term: we should recalc commitment sizing monthly with per-model percentile-based sizing (e.g., 95th token-hours per route) and add a small burst buffer (10%). Current static reservation is stale.
Oliver Chen: agree. Also add a per-model hourly breakdown in the finops dashboard (not just per-route). That helps teams own their model spend.
Maya Patel: action items: 1) disable burst for top 3 routes (Maya) 2) update dashboard short-window alert (Samir) 3) recalc EU reserved commitment proposal for next quarter with Raghav + Finance (Raghav + Finance Analyst).
Raghav Singh: will run utilization simulation after change and share numbers by EOD. If recalc shows needed commitment > 150 GPUh, we should push for a short-term add-on reservation to avoid on-demand spikes.
Finance Analyst: thanks — I'll hold on billing adjustments and sync with procurement. If we need add-on commitments, procurement lead will need a 2-week lead time for contract.
Samir Khan: FYI leave a note in the roadmap: implement per-model cost attribution in the service mesh (trace IDs -> billing tags). That will make future audits much faster.
Maya Patel: deploying patch now. will report back once burst disabled. :rocket:
Maya Patel: update — bursts disabled for the three routes at 03:25 UTC. early telemetry shows peak on-demand rate dropping ~70% within 10m.
Raghav Singh: got the simulation run — with burst off, 24h projected EU on-demand spend down by ~$3.6k. With a 10% buffer committed (commitment -> 132 GPUh) we cover expected 95th percentile and reduce monthly variability. Sharing spreadsheet: https://docs.redwood/finops/eu-commitment-sim
Finance Analyst: Case #BILL-4621 updated with mitigation notes and provisional cost reconciliation. We'll aim to have a final accounting in tomorrow's daily finops.
Samir Khan: great response team, closing loop after tomorrow morning's dashboard snapshot. :thumbsup:
